content.comment_body: Hello everyone! I'm working with a [product_name] PLC ([article_no]) and a [product_name] HMI ([article_no]) for a project. I also use [product_name] and [product_name] to program both devices. Everything was functioning well until I realized that none of my recipes were being saved in the permanent/retentive memory. After shutting down the PLC/HMI, all recipe values reset to their defaults. Can anyone assist? Thank you in advance, [user_name]
To address this, we'd need to see how recipe data transfers from the HMI to the PLC. Please upload your [product_name] program and the [product_name] project in a ZIP archive.

Hi! I've found that the issue was not a technical fault. When I simulated the HMI and modified graphic elements, the system recompiled the project each time, which caused recipes to be overwritten with their default values. Thanks nonetheless.

analysis.insight_summary: The user experienced what seemed to be a loss of recipe data in the HMI/PLC setup programmed with [product_name] tools. This was caused by repeated project compilations during simulation, which reset recipe data to default values—not due to an actual device malfunction. Users expect recipe modifications to be persistently stored and may be confused by deployment steps that reset data.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects recipe changes made via the HMI to remain in device retentive memory after shut down and restart.
